title: Stack overflow under webR when reading lines
description:
The code,

https://github.com/r-lib/brio/blob/e49991b6fd14db3590dce2c2ef9b106a02b7b7b5/src/read_lines.c#L56-L57

overflows the stack when running under webR. WebR's stack size is 1MB, but going over this does not immediately terminate. Instead we get subtle memory corruption issues later on.

Can we allocate a smaller `read_buf`, at the cost of more calls to `fread()` for larger files? I've tested 64K and that fixes the memory corruption under webR,

```c
#define READ_BUF_SIZE 64 * 1024 
```

There could also be an `ifdef` that kicks in just for Wasm,

```c
#ifdef __EMSCRIPTEN__
#define READ_BUF_SIZE 64 * 1024 
#else
#define READ_BUF_SIZE 1024 * 1024 
#endif
```

Otherwise, could `read_buf` be allocated on the heap instead?

I'm happy to submit a PR, just let me know which kind of change you think would be best.

title: Issue running tests on ARM
description:
From Andreas Tille

```
the R packaging team in Debian has packaged brio.  There is a CI
infrastructure which is running the test suite on several architectures.
The test suite runs nicely on Intel architectures.  However, there was
an issue with arm64, armhf and ppc64el (which are the only non-Intel
architectures currently so this list might not be complete).  The test
suite simply never ended and the tests were manually stopped by the
admins.

Yesterday I bisected the tests to find out what actual test is
responsible for the issue and I was successful with excluding a
single test[1].  So for whatever reason this code


test_that("file_line_endings detects Unix line endings", {
  tmp <- tempfile()
  on.exit(unlink(tmp))

  writeBin(charToRaw("foo\n"), tmp)

  expect_equal(file_line_endings(tmp), "\n")

  writeBin(charToRaw(""), tmp)

  expect_identical(file_line_endings(tmp), NA_character_)
})
```

title: Request: function for writing text as UTF-8, without appending a newline
description:
I have code which generates a string like this, and I'd like to write it to disk verbatim. If I write it to disk with `write_lines()`, an extra `\n` gets appended.

```R
gentext <- function() "abc\nxyz\n"

x <- gentext()
x
#> [1] "abc\nxyz\n"


write_lines(x, "temp.txt")
read_file("temp.txt")
#> [1] "abc\nxyz\n\n"
```

I would like to have a function which is fast and automatically encodes to UTF-8 like `write_lines()`, but which does not append an `\n` to the input.

My current solution is this, but it would be nice if something similar was in brio.

```R
write_utf8 <- function(text, ...) {
  writeBin(charToRaw(enc2utf8(text)), ...)
}
```
